title: Reliability Catalyst: Ops Prototype Brief
body:
Purpose:
This brief outlines a 10-week cross-functional pilot (the "Reliability Catalyst") to prototype an ops-integrated SLO program that can be rolled out org-wide. The goal is to validate coordination patterns, telemetry gating, and lightweight governance so product teams can adopt SLOs without heavy process overhead.

Summary of approach:
- Run a narrow, high-impact pilot across three services (chat-routing, embeddings-indexer, hosted-inference-proxy).
- Use an "experiment lane" model: each service owner runs a 4-6 week SLO experiment (choose thresholds, define metrics, test alerting & runbook).
- Platform provides an out-of-the-box SLO binding matrix, telemetry dashboards, and an error-budget reallocation mechanism.
- SRE + Platform + Product form a weekly triage cadence with decision rights for fallback and escalation.

Success criteria (prototype):
1) Measurable reduction in noise: at least 40% fewer actionable alerts per service from baseline in steady-state weeks.
2) SLO clarity: three service teams have documented SLOs, ownership, and runbooks in the Catalyst Confluence space.
3) Operational runway: platform integrates telemetry gating that can mute noisy signals for 72 hours without human intervention for known degradations.
4) Playbook time: mean time to runbook execution (from page to engaged owner with initial mitigation) under 15 mins for P1 incidents in pilot services.

High-level timeline (10 weeks):
- Week 0 (prep): finalize metrics, grant telemetry access, create SLO binding templates.
- Weeks 1-2 (discovery): baseline collection, service impact mapping, error-budget thresholds draft.
- Weeks 3-6 (experiment execution): implement SLOs, wire alerts, run simulated load/chaos windows, tune thresholds.
- Weeks 7-8 (stabilize): evaluate results, runbook rehearsals, integrate adaptive routing fallback tests.
- Weeks 9-10 (handoff): produce handoff artifacts, decision memo for org-wide rollout, list of required platform features.

Workstreams and owners:
- Program Lead: Carmen Liu (platform-engineering) — program coordination, external comms, decision memo.
- SRE Liasons: Diego Fernández, Tomoko Sato — oncall integration, alert tuning, incident postmortems.
- Observability: Aisha Patel — dashboards, telemetry gating logic, instrumentation guidance.
- Product Partners: Ben Carlson (hosted-api), Mira Shah (embeddings team), Kunal Desai (chat-routing) — SLO owners and experiment leads.
- Solutions/SE: Leah Morgan — customer-impact scenarios and external stakeholder comms.

Deliverables (per service):
- SLO definition doc (objective, SLI definitions, measurement windows).
- SLO binding matrix (which alerts map to which SLOs and which teams own them).
- Reduced-noise dashboard (baseline vs current alerts, top contributing signals).
- Runbook + escalation tree, and 2 tabletop rehearsal notes.

Telemetry gating & adaptive budget policies (prototype design notes):
- Telemetry gating: allow temporary suppression of noisy signals tied to a verified incident tag (e.g., "known-degradation:rolling-restart") for up to 72 hours, with automatic escalation to the SRE liaison if the tagged event exceeds 6 hours.
- Adaptive error-budget reallocation: service owners can request a one-time reallocation for maintenance windows through a lightweight approval channel (Slack approval by SRE liaison + one product lead). Requests are logged and automatically expire.
- Canary burn-in: traffic split to fall back model variants if estimation shows SLO breach risk > 60% during a rolling model rollout.

Communication plan:
- Weekly triage meeting (30 mins) — standing invite for program lead, sre liaisons, product partners, observability engineer. Agenda: signals, outstanding requests, approvals, blockers.
- Daily async short-form status in #reliability-catalyst (poster: SLO owners rotate daily updates).
- Stakeholder demo (end of week 6) — 20min demo of dashboards and chosen mitigations + 10min Q&A.
- Decision memo to execs (week 10) with recommended rollout path and platform investments.

Risk register (top items):
- Incomplete instrumentation: no-cardinality-safe metrics for a given SLI can delay the experiment. Mitigation: observability pre-checklist in Week 0.
- Alert escalation overload: teams may incorrectly map alerts to SLOs causing confusion. Mitigation: require SRE liaison signoff for initial mappings.
- Policy churn: adaptive budget rules could be misused. Mitigation: require timeboxed approvals and audit logs in Confluence.

Integration points and dependencies:
- Telemetry platform: needs to expose SLI-level rollups, anomaly scores, and rule-based gating endpoints (work with observability infra).
- Incident management: PagerDuty routing must support temporary routing rules for the three pilot services.
- Feature flags: platform release infra must support traffic-splitting for canary burn-in tests.
- Compliance/legal: any change to retention of telemetry or audit logs flagged to security for review (linked_artifacts contain compliance checklist).

Lightweight templates attached (to be copied into each service space):
- SLO one-pager template (objective, SLI measurement, error budget calc, owners, comms).
- Runbook template (symptoms, impact, mitigation steps, rollback, postmortem prompts).
- Approval note template for maintenance/reallocation requests.

Open questions / decisions needed by Week 0:
1) Who approves one-off error budget reallocation (SRE lead or product VP)?
2) What is the canonical SLI aggregation window for the hosted-inference-proxy (60s, 5m, 1h)?
3) Can platform expose gating endpoints that will be used by product teams without extra quota costs?

Quick next steps (action list):
- Carmen: circulate this brief and set Week 0 prep meeting (by 2026-05-15).
- Aisha: run observability pre-checks for the three pilot services and publish the checklist in the Catalyst Confluence space (by 2026-05-18).
- SRE liaisons: draft initial alert-to-SLO mapping for each pilot service and flag gaps (by 2026-05-20).

Notes to self (working):
- Keep scope small: pick services with high customer impact but limited cross-deps.
- Emphasize reversible changes: prefer gating and routing knobs over heavy infra changes in the prototype.
- Track qualitative feedback (team friction, ramp difficulty) as a first-class metric for rollout readiness.

Appendix: example SLO binding matrix (abbreviated)
- hosted-inference-proxy: latency_p95 <= 1200ms (window 5m) -> alerts: backend-latency-95, queue-backpressure -> owner: hosted-api product + SRE liaison Diego.
- embeddings-indexer: availability >= 99.8% (window 7d) -> alerts: db-replica-error-rate, consumer-lag-high -> owner: embeddings product + SRE liaison Tomoko.
- chat-routing: correctness SLA (reroute rate <= 0.5% per day) -> alerts: routing-fallbacks, model-timeout -> owner: chat team + SRE liaison Diego.

End of brief.

(Working doc: expect iterations. Attachments: SLO template, runbook template, experiment tracker spreadsheet TBD.)
